pipeline.label: The Pipeline Architecture
pipeline.title: The Verification Thread
pipeline.desc: Every answer is tethered to its source, start to finish. Raw filings become verifiable legal intelligence through six stages.
pipeline.stage1Desc: Judgments, orders, and case files ingested as PDF, DOCX, or scanned image — no reformatting required.
pipeline.stage2Desc: Layout-aware OCR reconstructs paragraphs, tables, and cause-title structure from scanned court records.
pipeline.stage3Desc: Passages are split at legal boundaries and tagged for judges, sections, acts, and dates.
pipeline.stage4Desc: Vector embeddings and lexical (BM25) indexes are built side by side for meaning and exact statute matches.
pipeline.stage5Desc: Retrieved passages ground every generated answer — the model argues from your corpus, not memory.
pipeline.stage6Desc: Each claim is traced back to its source paragraph before it ever reaches the researcher.

capabilities.label: System Capabilities
capabilities.title: Built for how legal research actually happens.
capabilities.card1Desc: Ask in plain language — "cases where anticipatory bail was denied under Section 438" — and retrieve ranked judgments by meaning, not just keyword.
capabilities.card2Desc: Multi-page orders condensed into facts, issues, holding, and ratio — each line traceable to its paragraph.
capabilities.card3Desc: Judges, counsel, acts, sections, and dates auto-tagged across every document you upload.
capabilities.card4Desc: Cross-reference old Penal Code sections against the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita instantly, with mapping confidence shown inline.

workspace.label: The NyayaSarathi Workspace
workspace.title: Read the judgment. Verify the answer. Same screen.
workspace.desc: Click any highlighted citation in the Research Note to jump straight to its source paragraph in the document pane.
workspace.searchPlaceholder: What did the Court hold about delay in FIR filing under Section 420?
workspace.docCourt: Supreme Court of India · Criminal Appeal 1142/2019
workspace.docPara14: In the matter of Section 420, this Court has consistently held that mere delay in lodging the First Information Report does not, by itself, vitiate the prosecution's case, provided the delay is satisfactorily explained by the complainant on record.
workspace.docPara15: Justice A.K. Rao, delivering the opinion of the bench, observed that the trial court correctly appreciated the testimony of PW-3 in light of the surrounding circumstances dated 14 March 2018.
workspace.docPara18: The appellant's counsel contended that the delay of eleven days was fatal to the case, relying on precedent under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
workspace.docPara21: This Court, relying on the settled position under Section 154, CrPC, finds that the explanation tendered was consistent and credible, and accordingly affirms the conviction recorded by the courts below.
workspace.docPara24: For the foregoing reasons, the appeal fails and is dismissed, with the sentence awarded by the Trial Court, as affirmed by the High Court, standing undisturbed.
workspace.answerLine1: The Court held that mere delay in lodging an FIR, by itself,
workspace.answerLine2: does not vitiate the prosecution’s case
workspace.answerLine3: where the delay stands satisfactorily explained on record.
workspace.answerLine4: This finds direct support in the reasoning applied by the bench
workspace.answerLine5: in its interpretation of Section 154, CrPC.
